title: Conversational Graph Schema and Proxy Draft
content:
Objective:
Small personal draft for a compact, portable conversational-graph schema and a lightweight proxy that sits between client SDKs and Redwood’s hosted/dedicated runtime. Goal is to capture enough topology to support: partial replay, checkpoint diffs, multi-tool routing, and eviction-friendly KV caching while keeping wire shape compact for mobile/edge clients.

Rationale / motivation:
- We need a stable compact format that clients can serialize to disk and send as a delta to the server on resume.
- Avoid shipping entire token history; allow prefix anchors + sparse deltas.
- Keep proxy logic simple so it can live in mobile SDKs or edge sidecars.

Core concepts (informal):
- Node: a single turn or structural object (system/assistant/user/tool-result/embedding-anchor).
- Edge: ordering or causal link (previous->next, tool-call->tool-result).
- Anchor: a compact representation of a long prefix (sha256 id + summary tokens + kv-hash).
- Patch: a delta that attaches nodes or re-anchors an existing branch.
- Affinity tags: lightweight labels to indicate routing preference (fast-path, cached, privacy-controlled).

Wire shape (JSON-ish, intentionally compact fields):
- graph_id: string (uuid v4)
- root_anchor: string? (optional anchor id)
- nodes: [ { id, t, role, tok_count, anchor_refs?, meta? } ]
  - id: short base62 id (e.g. aZv9)
  - t: type single letter (u=user, a=assistant, s=system, r=tool-result, e=embed)
  - role: free text role label (optional)
  - tok_count: integer estimate (helps routing/hinting)
  - anchor_refs: [anchor_id] (if node is summarized)
  - meta: map flattened into "k=v;..." to keep small (see examples)
- edges: [ { from, to, rel } ]  (rel: "next", "calls", "refines")
- anchors: [ { id, digest, summary_tokens_base64, kv_index_digest } ]
- patches: [ { patch_id, add_nodes?, add_edges?, reanchor_ops? } ]
- affinity: ["fast-path","no-cache","gdpr-scope=eu"]

Example minimal payload (handy for mobile resume):
{
  "graph_id":"f3e2-...",
  "root_anchor":"anc:9f3a",
  "nodes":[{"id":"n1","t":"s","role":"conversation-start","tok_count":12,"meta":"lang=en"},{"id":"n2","t":"u","tok_count":8}],
  "edges":[{"from":"n1","to":"n2","rel":"next"}],
  "anchors":[{"id":"anc:9f3a","digest":"sha256:...","summary_tokens_base64":"SGVsbG8g...","kv_index_digest":"kvid:2b7"}],
  "affinity":["fast-path"]
}

API sketch: client -> proxy -> runtime controller
- POST /v1/conv/graphs (create)
  - body: graph minimal payload (optionally with full nodes)\  - returns: graph_id, accepted_anchor_ids, server_policy (eviction_ttl, cache_hint)
- PATCH /v1/conv/graphs/:id (patch)
  - body: patch (patch_id, nodes, edges, reanchor instructions)\  - optimistic sync: if patch_id conflict -> return conflict_token + diff range
- POST /v1/conv/graphs/:id/resolve (resolve for inference)
  - body: { root_pointer, target_token_budget, routing_affinity[] }\  - returns: signed session_token that encodes which anchors are trusted and a short provenance blob
- GET /v1/conv/graphs/:id?/anchors/:aid (fetch anchor)\  - for edge clients to fetch specific anchor summaries on demand

Proxy responsibilities (lightweight):
- Maintain an LRU of anchors (configurable by total token budget).
- Stitch local partial graphs with server patches; emit compact patches to runtime.
- Validate anchor digests and fetch missing anchors lazily.
- Expose a tiny policy DSL for client privacy: e.g. allowAnchors=[local-only,server-sync], redactFields=[meta.kv]

Runtime server responsibilities:
- Expand anchors into full token sequences (if server has long-term storage), or reject with fetch suggestion.
- Verify provenance signatures (if provided) to prevent tampering of affinity tags in high-privilege flows.
- Provide guidance: suggested quantization profile + batch placement (e.g., recommend 8k vs 32k model variant) based on tok_count heuristics.

Local cache eviction policy (sketch):
- Score(anchor) = freshness_score * (1 + hit_rate_weight) / (tok_count ^ 0.5)
- Freshness_score decays linearly over TTL window.
- If eviction results in lost anchor referenced by a pending patch, mark pending patch as "stalled" and retry fetch sequence.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Do we include a small protobuf variant for mobile to reduce size vs JSON? Pros: smaller, faster. Cons: harder to iterate during early dev. (leaning protobuf for release; keep JSON first for experiments)
- Anchors: should they include a short semantic fingerprint (embedding) to allow similarity-based cache hits? Privacy implications if embeddings leak. Maybe hash the embedding with client-specific salt.
- How do we sign anchors for on-device private anchors vs server-canonical anchors? E2E signing or HMAC? Key rotation flow must be simple.
- Conflict resolution semantics for concurrent patches from multi-clients (desktop + mobile). Strategy: vector-clock-lite + last-writer-preferred for non-critical metadata, but use merge strategies for node sequence.
- How large should base62 ids be to avoid collisions across distributed offline generation? 10 chars? 8 chars? Possibly include graph_id prefix.

Security & privacy notes:
- Sensitive nodes (PII) should be tagged meta="sensitive=pii" and proxied with policy header x-privacy:hold. Proxy must refrain from uploading sensitive anchors unless explicit user opt-in.
- Anchor digests should not reveal content; only store sha256 and optionally redact summary string.

Edge cases / failure modes:
- Partial anchor fetch fails mid-inference -> runtime should fall back to short-context path (truncate to last N nodes) and emit a degrade metric.
- Concurrent reanchoring while a session token is being used -> token invalidation must be cheap: issue short-lived session tokens and allow refresh endpoint.

Implementation notes / next steps (developer checklist):
- [ ] Write compact JSON schema and small proto spec side-by-side (proto file + json schema).
- [ ] Implement a reference proxy library (ts, go) with LRU anchor cache and simple policy DSL.
- [ ] Add unit tests for patch conflict resolution (vector-clock-lite).
- [ ] Bake-in telemetry counters: anchor_fetch_latency, anchor_miss_rate, patch_conflict_rate, policy_blocked_uploads.
- [ ] Draft integration experiment with hosted API (create a small canary route that accepts graph payloads and returns session_token).

Notes-to-self (quick brainstorm snippets):
- Maybe allow "synthetic anchors" created server-side that summarize multiple branches into cluster anchors (useful for long multi-turn threads).
- Consider a "compact diff" encoding that is token-level run-length encoded to save size for repeated text.
- Keep the meta string simple to avoid nested JSON; trick: use semicolon-separated key=val pairs to preserve flatness and parsing simplicity in tiny mobile libs.

References / related tickets:
- JIRA-COG-1423: "graph-based context resume" (design umbrella)
- PR runtime#718: initial server-side anchor index prototype
- Slack: #eng-runtime thread started Aug 2 2025 with initial sketches

If this becomes useful, split into two docs: schema.proto + proxy-reference-TS.md. For now keep as single scratchpad.

End.
